title: Terroir Roast — Burlap Slab Declaration
description: A specialty-coffee origin card built around a hessian-textured ground, a confident slab-serif origin name, and a one-colour coffee-cherry illustration — closer to a roastery bag than a slide deck.
philosophy: This template exists for brands that treat provenance as poetry. It borrows wholesale from the visual language of single-origin packaging — raw woven texture, restrained corner illustration, assertive display type — and refuses the polished gradients and icon grids that flatten craft into commodity. The speaker is a roaster, a green buyer, or a coffee educator who believes the name of a cooperative deserves to fill the frame. The audience leans in; the room should smell like espresso.
goodFor: Single-origin coffee or cacao farm reveal slides
Artisan food and beverage brand story decks
Roastery or farm-to-cup origin education sessions
Horizontal tasting-note lists of 3–6 short descriptors
avoidFor: SaaS or fintech product pitch decks
Multi-column data tables and KPI dashboards
Brands requiring a clean, texture-free digital-native aesthetic
author: harness

examples.promptCore: Tactile and reverential, the slide should feel like a craft roastery's micro-lot bag propped against a worn wooden counter — raw woven ground filling the frame with quiet authority. The origin name commands the composition with almost uncomfortable confidence, while a single coffee-cherry motif anchors the lower corner, keeping the layout asymmetric and earthy. A sparse provenance line below reads like a whispered annotation. Avoid polished gradients, symmetrical icon arrangements, or any corporate slide chrome — this should feel hand-stamped and printed, never digitally rendered.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed burlap texture covers the entire slide — no white margins, no panel borders, no header band. On a 12-col grid, the primary origin or brand name occupies cols 2–10, sitting in the upper-center third of the frame with a thin rule line beneath it separating it from a short provenance tagline below. A single coffee-cherry illustration bleeds off the lower-right corner at roughly 25% of slide width, acting as a counterweight to the left-anchored text mass. A small deck identifier or year floats bottom-left, set in spaced small caps, providing the only structural footer element.

examples.promptCore: The slide evokes the back panel of a specialty roastery bag — tactile, unhurried, confident in restraint. A woven hessian ground anchors the composition with organic imperfection; a single illustrative motif is the only decorative flourish. Tasting descriptors are separated by thin rule lines rather than bullet points, giving each word room to land as a sensory cue. Refuse gradient overlays, icon rows, or symmetrical grid logic — the mood should feel hand-curated, never templated.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with primary content in cols 2–10; a large display origin word or cooperative name anchors the upper-left, spanning roughly half the column width. Tasting descriptors run as a horizontal, rule-divided list in the lower third — spaced generously, no bullets. A single-colour coffee-cherry illustration is clipped to the upper-right corner, occupying roughly one quarter of the total slide area. No header band; a subdued lot or harvest code sits bottom-left, with outer margins breathing at 6–7% on all sides.
